subject: TechScale evaluation — post-call recap & benchmark plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Eric Hsu <eric.hsu@techscale.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2028 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: TechScale evaluation — post-call recap & benchmark plan

Eric — thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Current ask / priority (from TechScale):
- Understand real-world latency and throughput differences between Redwood and the hyperscaler endpoints you currently use for inference.
- Focus on p95/p99 latencies for interactive flows and sustained tokens/sec for bulk inference.

2) What we committed on the call:
- A lightweight A/B benchmark that mirrors your 3 canonical flows (chat assist, long-form summarization, batch embeddings).
- Measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1K-tokens for each run.
- Run Redwood baseline vs your current endpoints (SkyBridge) and a second hyperscaler (AsterCloud) if you want broader context.

3) Logistics & proposed timeline:
- We’ll share a lab plan (attached) with test harness, sample prompts, and data handling notes — aim to kick off next week (Mon/Tue) and deliver preliminary results in 5 business days.
- We need a single service account from TechScale with a limited test corpus and the three representative prompt sets.

4) Open questions from our team: 
- Can you confirm target concurrency for interactive tests (estimated 8–16 concurrent users)?
- Any token limits or custom truncation rules we should emulate?

Attachments: techscale-bench-plan.xlsx (test matrix), redwood-interop-checklist.pdf (privacy & network notes)

Next step: I’ll follow up with the lab plan and a one-page checklist for your infra team. If the timeline looks tight for you, tell us preferred start date.

—
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

From: Eric Hsu <eric.hsu@techscale.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@cloudops.tech>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2028 18:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TechScale evaluation — post-call recap & benchmark plan

Neha — thanks, that summary looks right. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: for live chat we typically see 12 concurrent sessions during peak. Happy to have you use 12 as the target.
- Token handling: we have a soft truncate at 2048 tokens on the input; beyond that we apply semantic chunking. Important to replicate.
- AsterCloud is fine — we already have an account there and can provide creds for the tests.

We’ll provision the limited service account by end of day Friday and share the three prompt sets. Question: can you instrument the run to capture downstream cold-starts vs warmed container behavior? That matters for our synthetic-to-production translation.

Best,
Eric
Head of Platform Engineering, TechScale
eric.hsu@techscale.io | +1 (206) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Eric Hsu <eric.hsu@techscale.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Oct 2028 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TechScale evaluation — post-call recap & benchmark plan

Eric / Neha — adding a couple technical constraints and the exact metrics we plan to collect so everyone's clear: 

Planned A/B tests (high level):
- Interactive chat flow (12 concurrent sessions): 1000 short-turn dialogs (avg 60 tokens output) — measure p50/p95/p99 per request and tokens/sec sustained over 10-minute windows.
- Long-form summarization: 200 requests with ~3k input tokens (simulate chunking behavior); measure end-to-end completion time and p99 for multi-chunk orchestration.
- Bulk embeddings: 100k rows processed in batches of 512 — report tokens/sec, throughput (rows/sec), and cost per 1k rows.

Metrics we'll capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail jitter, tokens/sec (moving avg), percent of requests served under 300ms/500ms thresholds (interactive), cost-per-1k-tokens, and cold-start rate. We'll tag runs as warmed vs cold.

About cold-starts: we will run a dedicated cold-start sweep (N=30) for each provider and flag the distribution. That will let you see worst-case p99s during scale events.

Data collection & test harness:
- We'll use a lightweight harness that emits request traces to a shared S3 bucket and a perf dashboard (link in Drive).
- We need your team to allow outbound connections to our test endpoints and provide creds for SkyBridge + AsterCloud.

I attached a skeleton CSV of the prompt set and the bench matrix in the plan. If you want, Karthik and I can do a 30-minute sync with your infra ops team to walk through the checklist before we start.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — short update and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Kickoff timing: TechScale-provided creds + prompt sets received by EOD Monday (we understand you'll provision by Friday — appreciate that). We’ll start the harness on Tuesday morning (PST) and run the initial sweep through Friday.

2) Deliverables:
- Preliminary perf dashboard (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec) within 72 hours of test start.
- Full deliverable with annotated artifacts (CSV traces, cost calc, interpretation) within 5 business days.

3) Action items assigned: 
- TechScale: service account + prompt sets + confirmation of concurrency (Eric / Priya)
- Redwood (Marissa / Karthik): finalize harness, add cold-start sweep, map SkyBridge/AsterCloud configs to Redwood equivalents.
- Redwood (Neha): run a short alignment call with your infra ops on Monday to validate firewall/egress rules (15–20m).

4) Quick notes on differentiators we’ll highlight in the report: predictable p99 under sustained concurrency (routing + KV cache), explicit tokens/sec controls, and per-route cost breakdowns. We’ll surface any quantization impact we observe for long-form jobs.

If this plan works, I’ll schedule the 15m infra alignment call for Monday at 10am PT — let me know if another slot is better.

Attachments referenced: techscale-bench-plan.xlsx, redwood-interop-checklist.pdf

—
